Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The Sri Lanka Women players are in a huddle, where skipper Chamari Athapaththu is giving them a last-minute pep talk. Then they spread out to take their respective field positions. Pratika Rawal and Smriti Mandhana are the two openers for India Women. Malki Madara to start proceedings with the ball.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then! It seems that India Women should cruise through in the chase but a reminder that Sri Lanka Women are coming with a spin-heavy attack and they know better than anyone who to bowl on home conditions. If they pick 2-3 wickets in the first 10 overs, we should be in for a treat. Stay tuned for the chase.

India read the conditions brilliantly and did a good job of bowling first under wonderful conditions. Their pacers got just one wicket in the first Powerplay but executed the plans well. Then the spinners came in and did their job fluently to build up more pressure, they regularly picked wickets and never allowed the opposition to get on the front foot. Deepti Sharma, Sneh Rana and Shree Charani, all three spinners took 7 wickets together and dismantled the Lankan batting order quite easily.

A tough outing for the Lankan batters as they struggled throughout the innings. Under overcast conditions, the Lankan batters found it hard to face the Indian pacers. Chamari Athapaththu was always going to be key for them while batting, but she fell cheaply, and the onus was on the other batters to do the job. Hasini Perera played a handy innings at the top, but for Sri Lanka Women, quite a few often went into a shell where scoring runs was hard, and that just resulted in a lot of pressure, which eventually turned into wickets. Kavisha Dilhari, Anushka Sanjeewani, and Achini Kulasuriya all got off to a start but struggled a lot to rotate the strike regularly.

OUT! TAKEN SUPERBLY IN THE DEEP! Deepti Sharma wraps things up and ends Sri Lanka Women's agony. This is tossed up, full and on off, Achini Kulasuriya goes down for the slog sweep but has to drag it and mistimes it. The ball flies towards deep mid-wicket, where Jemimah Rodrigues runs a long way forward and dives to take a stunning catch. That caps off an amazing bowling display for India Women as they have bowled out the hosts for just 147.

Commentary.Commentary: After a long rain delay, we are finally set to begin! The players are already out in the middle. Hasini Perera and Chamari Athapaththu are the two openers for Sri Lanka Women. Debutant Kashvee Gautam has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

Chamari Athapaththu, the captain of Sri Lanka Women, says that they would have bowled first as well. Adds that they want to play positive cricket, and any score above 200 will be a good one. Informs that they also have two debutants in the team - Malki Madara and Piumi Badalge.

Harmanpreet Kaur, the skipper of India Women, says that they will bowl first because of the weather conditions. Adds that they are very excited about the opportunity to play in this series. Informs that they have two debutants in Kashvee Gautam and Shree Charani.

PITCH REPORT - Gamini Perera is near the pitchside. He says the ground staff have lived up to their expectation for the work they have done despite so much rain. Looking at the pitch, Perera says it is pretty hard, it will be hard for the spinners to generate turn. Reckons there is a lot of moisture, and due to the overcast conditions, the pacers could get some conventional swing.

Sri Lanka Women (Playing XI) - Chamari Athapaththu (C), Hasini Perera, Harshitha Samarawickrama, Kavisha Dilhari, Nilakshika Silva, Anushka Sanjeewani (WK), Hansima Karunaratne, Piumi Badalge, Achini Kulasuriya, Inoka Ranaweera, Malki Madara.

India Women (Playing XI) - Smriti Mandhana, Pratika Rawal, Harleen Deol, Harmanpreet Kaur (C),  Jemimah Rodrigues, Richa Ghosh (WK), Deepti Sharma, Kashvee Gautam, Arundhati Reddy, Sneh Rana, Shree Charani.
TOSS - India Women have won the toss and elected to BOWL first.

UPDATE - The moment we were waiting for is finally here as the official word is in now. The toss will happen in a bit, and 'THE MATCH WILL BEGIN AT 12 PM IST (6.30 AM GMT). Also, it will be a 39-overs-per-side game.

UPDATE - 11.15 am IST (5.45 am GMT) - Most of the covers are off now except for a couple near the boundary ropes. They started from the middle so that the water on the covers doesn't spill on the outfield which was a smart thing to do. Now, with no rain, and the groundstaff doing an amazing job, we should have an official update sooner rather than later.

UPDATE - 10.56 am IST (5.26 am GMT) - Good news! The rain has stopped completely and the groundsmen are slowly peeling the covers off. It will take some time as the whole ground is under the blue sheet but a lot of optimistic signs from Colombo. Stay tuned.

UPDATE - 10.46 am IST (5.16 GMT) - The drizzle is back on in Colombo, and even though it is very light, the entire ground remains covered. We have now had a delay of over 45 minutes, and that means, we have started to lose overs too. Let's hope we get to see some cricket even if it is a shortened game.

UPDATE - 10.20 am IST (4.50 am GMT) - Some positive news! The rain has stopped, but the covers are still firmly on and there is a lot of water on them. The biggest concern are the water puddles on the outfield and the groundstaff will need a lot of time to prepare the ground for action. Fingers crossed!

UPDATE - 10 am IST (4.30 am GMT) - It's not just raining, it is absolutely pouring down now and a few puddles have also started to form which is never a good sign. The forecast looks pretty gloomy, not just for this game, but for the entire next week in Colombo. However, we still remain hopeful that we will get some action. Stick with us for more news.

UPDATE - 9.41 am IST (4.11 am GMT) - If you are wondering why the toss hasn't happened yet, it is because it's raining in Colombo and the covers are firmly on the ground. 'TOSS HAS BEEN OFFICIALLY DELAYED'. Stay tuned for further updates.

India Women on the other hand are one of the favourites for the World Cup and to win this series as well. Led by Harmanpreet Kaur, she have under her arsenal almost a full recognisable experienced squad with a couple of new additions. However, in this series, Renuka Singh Thakur, Pooja Vastrakar, and Titas Sadhu all ruled out due to injuries so we might see a different bowling attack, maybe more spin dominating as pitch tends to support spinners in Sri Lanka. Also, the forecast remains a bit dull in Colombo as there are possibilities of rain affecting the match. Let’s hope we get an exciting series to watch. Stay tuned for the toss and other updates.

The 2025 Women’s ODI World Cup is on the horizon and teams have started their preparations in full flow. Sri Lanka, the home team have recently flourished in this format thanks to their captain Chamari Athapaththu’s leadership style but to make an impact on the upcoming World Cup, there is no better opportunity than this series.

Hello and welcome to the first match of the Women’s Tri-Nation series between India Women and Sri Lanka Women. The franchise cricket have taken all the headlines recently but the international cricket is slowly coming back in action and with that comes Women’s Cricket as well. South Africa are the third team who’ll play the series but today it’s time for the two Asian teams to take the field.
...MATCH DAY...

The countdown to the 2025 Women’s ODI World Cup is well and truly on, and with the recently concluded Qualifier, all eight teams have now secured their place at the global event. As part of their preparations, Sri Lanka, India, and South Africa are set to face off in a Tri-series. The series will follow a double round-robin format, with the top two teams at the end of the league stage advancing to the final. All matches will be hosted at the R Premadasa Stadium in Colombo, with the opening clash featuring the hosts, Sri Lanka, taking on their Asian rivals, India. Sri Lanka’s most recent ODI assignment came in New Zealand, where their batting came under pressure. Back on home soil, the hosts will be eager to bounce back. As expected, Chamari Athapaththu will lead the charge with the bat, supported by the likes of Vishmi Gunarathne, Harshitha Samarawickrama, and Nilakshika Silva. The Islanders have named a spin-heavy bowling unit, spearheaded by Sugandika Kumari and Inoka Ranaweera, with Inoshi Priyadharshani and the uncapped Dewmi Vihanga rounding off a varied spin contingent. Rashmika Sewwandi and Manudi Nanayakkara, who were part of Sri Lanka's Under-19 World Cup squad, also find a place in the squad. Kavisha Dilhari stands out among the all-rounders and will play a key role with both bat and ball. However, the hosts will be without their experienced left-arm seamer Udeshika Prabodhani, who misses out due to injury. In her absence, the pace attack responsibilities will fall on Hansima Karunaratne and Achini Kulasuriya. As for India, they had an ODI series against the West Indies and Ireland on either side of the new year, but have since had a long gap from 50-over cricket. Harmanpreet Kaur will lead the side, with Smriti Mandhana, Jemimah Rodrigues, Harleen Deol, and Pratika Rawal forming the core of the batting unit. The Women in Blue boast a versatile group of all-rounders in Deepti Sharma, Sneh Rana, Arundhati Reddy, and Amanjot Kaur. The latest addition to the squad is Kashvee Gautam, who has been rewarded for her standout performances in the Women’s T20 League. The left-arm spin duo of Shree Charani and Shuchi Upadhyay, both of whom impressed on the domestic circuit, are also exciting inclusions. With Renuka Singh Thakur, Pooja Vastrakar, and Titas Sadhu all ruled out due to injuries, India will have to rely heavily on their all-rounders to contribute with the ball as well. India have historically dominated Sri Lanka in the ODI format, but the Islanders will draw confidence from their stunning victory over India in the T20 Asia Cup final last year. Who are you backing to start their campaign with a win?
